title: Blush Still-Life — DTC Skincare Square
description: A strict 1:1 Instagram ad frame anchored by a single hero product shot on a warm blush ground, a maximum 6-word benefit headline, and a wordmark-plus-CTA footer. Separates itself from editorial templates through safe-area discipline and the DTC brand grammar of restraint.
philosophy: This template was built for brands that earn trust through quietness — one product, one truth, one nudge. It refuses multi-benefit copy stacks, refuses anything placed above the product that competes for the eye, and refuses the busyness that discount brands use to hide weak product stories. It is calibrated for a thumb-stopping pause on a feed, not a reading moment. The ideal speaker is a product photographer who understands that negative space functions as body copy.
goodFor: Paid social square placements for DTC beauty or wellness brands
6-word benefit callout ads requiring instant legibility
Brand awareness frames where the product itself is the visual anchor
avoidFor: Event, webinar, or service-based promotion slides
Landscape or widescreen placements where 1:1 safe-area logic breaks
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a product photographer's final edit: one pristine object suspended in warm, luminous quiet, surrounded by so much breathing room that the silence itself reads as premium. Compositional rhythm is vertical and centered-with-intention — the product is the undisputed anchor, the headline is a whisper beneath it, and the footer is a polite gesture rather than a demand. Evoke the restraint of high-end apothecary shelf displays — matte, unhurried, confident. Avoid any diagonal energy, drop shadows that compete, or secondary graphic elements that imply busyness or discount-brand urgency.

examples.layoutNotes: Strict 1:1 canvas with an 8% safe-area inset on all four sides — nothing bleeds. 12-column grid; product photograph occupies cols 3–10 and sits at the vertical golden-section point (~38% from top), leaving the upper zone entirely empty. A single benefit headline (max 6 words) is set flush-left in cols 2–8 below the product, separated by a generous gap. Wordmark left-aligned and a pill-shaped CTA right-aligned form a locked footer strip pinned to the bottom safe-area edge — no page number, no header band.

examples.promptCore: A still, sun-warmed atmosphere — the feeling of a beauty counter caught in unhurried morning light, quiet and assured. The product is the sole protagonist; ground and space recede softly around it rather than competing. Compositional rhythm moves in one clean vertical gesture: object, then word, then action — nothing interrupts the descent. Avoid decorative texture accumulation, avoid any visual event placed above the product that competes for the eye, and avoid any density that reads as effort rather than earned confidence.

examples.layoutNotes: Strict 1:1 square canvas with a consistent safe-area inset on all four sides — no element bleeds or crops. The hero product occupies roughly the upper two-thirds of the frame, centered on its own vertical axis with deliberate negative space flanking both sides. The benefit headline sits beneath the product in a single short line, flush-left aligned to the safe-area edge, with generous breathing room above and below. A hairline rule or subtle tonal shift marks the bottom footer band, which holds the brand wordmark to the left and a compact pill-style CTA to the right.
